analysis: Documentation-only PR; no code changes visible. (1) docs/provider/hardware-requirements.md head lines 13-15 add a statement that Nemotron Super VL has no qualified RAM tier and is an internal, unregistered native builder path; it is a conservative claim and does not alter the load gate, serving authorization or the T-056/TB-011 qualification posture. (2) docs/reference/README.md adds a link to nemotron-super-image-formats.md. That target file is not in the supplied units, so I could not review its content or whether it exists (coverage limit). (3) docs/reference/configuration.md adds four env vars: DARKBLOOM_NEMOTRON_SUPER_MTP, _MTP_DEPTH, _MTP_VERIFICATION and _MAX_CONCURRENT. All are opt-in or default 1, and the docs state that invalid values fail the load, that MTP and concurrency above 1 are mutually exclusive, that the speculating owner refuses media, and that the KV grant must hold each request's fixed bytes. The docs say _MAX_CONCURRENT and _MTP are not forwarded to LaunchAgents; _DEPTH and _VERIFICATION are ignored unless MTP is 1. Residual concerns worth a later pass if the source changes are in other batches: a batched text decode with up to 64 concurrent requests relates to cross-request isolation and prefix-cache behavior (T-041 salt scoping, T-028 residual GPU/KV data) and memory-admission DoS (T-010, T-029). The visible docs claim row-exact batching and per-request KV accounting, but this cannot be verified from the supplied text. No threat-model assets, boundaries or mitigations are contradicted by the documented changes. The 'Last updated' dates were bumped without altering any security claim.
